sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed two-period panel sampling from \(P\). Population analysis distinguishes the proceedings paper's Assumptions 1--4 completion class from the bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class used for the positive sharp characterization.
sampling_model.units: Each superpopulation unit has observed \(Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2\) and one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\). Conditional parallel trends in the sensitivity class is imposed through jointly measurable versions on one common full-probability event for every baseline dose, which makes evaluation at \(d=X\) legitimate. The source supplies only the per-dose condition; the common-event diagonal clause is an explicit strengthening.
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline and follow-up doses are continuous and exact stayers are excluded. The sensitivity sharpness theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the support version \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause. On an observed law satisfying the source assumptions, the reported finite interval concerns only completions satisfying these additional restrictions and does not transfer upward to the unrestricted source class.
sampling_model.overlap: Population sensitivity analysis allows arbitrary compact observed support \(H\). Baseline-conditional zero support is sufficient for singleton recovery but is not required for the interval characterization. Uniform inference fixes a known finite rectangle union \(H\), assumes \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0\), and requires \(A\ge a_0\); these restrictions exclude support topology approaching failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is combined with the signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program. The event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) yields uniform outer coverage and the proved excess-endpoint rate. A matching lower bound remains open for fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\); shrinking support holes require a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula; the regular witness shows that this singleton is not identified over that published class.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimators admit uniform Gaussian approximations and confidence bands.
Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes.

body.tldr: Marginal quasi-stayers do not identify the weighted WAOSS singleton claimed by de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): at a regular heterogeneous-baseline witness, the published completion class contains an affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is all of \(\mathbb R\). The positive result is instead a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure. Its completion class adds a finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, a continuous support version of \(g\), and a simultaneous common-event parallel-trends clause needed on the random diagonal. Marginal quasi-stayers are not required for this characterization, and its finite attained obstacle interval does not transfer to the unrestricted source class. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton formula; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 remains an analogous result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The finite outer program yields a uniformly honest interval on the fixed-support regular subclass, while fixed-support minimaxity as \(R(P)\to0\) remains open.

project_justification.gap: The proceedings paper states weighted WAOSS point identification under Assumptions 1--4, but marginal quasi-stayers do not imply the baseline-conditional positivity invoked immediately before display (4) of its Appendix proof. The regular witness gives a generic-class certificate of failure: the published completion class admits a legal affine recession ray whose WAOSS image is \(\mathbb R\). The source's per-dose parallel-trends clause also does not by itself license evaluation at the random diagonal dose; the sensitivity model therefore states its simultaneous common-event strengthening explicitly.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates three objects that cannot be conflated: the unrestricted published class, which is unbounded at the witness; a bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class with continuous \(g\) and a simultaneous diagonal clause, which has an exact finite obstacle interval; and the baseline-conditional zero-support regime, in which that interval collapses to the published weighted formula. On source-admissible observed laws, only the source completions also satisfying the added sensitivity restrictions are being characterized; no global class equality or inclusion is asserted.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the source-class recession-ray counterexample and then characterizes the strengthened sensitivity class by a full-observed-law affine lift, attained interval geometry, the exact criterion \(R(P)=0\), conditional-support singleton recovery, obstacle compatibility and constant-one clipping, certified finite programs, and uniform outer coverage on a fixed rectangle-support subclass. The common-zero-baseline scalar interval from arXiv:2405.04465v4 is retained solely as prior-art validation, and the source paper's separate parametric estimator is outside the challenge.

body.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix argument immediately before display (4)) state a weighted WAOSS singleton under marginal quasi-stayers, although the proof invokes baseline-conditional positivity. The accepted source-class recession-ray proposition shows that the issue is substantive: at the regular witness the published completion class generates every value in \(\mathbb R\). Only this non-representability result transfers directly to that class. The positive finite interval is a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after the published singleton failure; it adds a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), and a simultaneous common-event parallel-trends clause. Under baseline-conditional zero support it collapses to the proceedings paper's weighted formula. Section 4.1, Assumption 5, and Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 provide an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval of de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, arXiv:2405.04465v4, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2) is prior art used only as an algebraic sanity check. Shape-restricted optimization and inference references motivate the computation, but the proved band-to-program theorem supplies the composition here. The proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated, and no current result supplies the open fixed-support minimax lower bound.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive identified set is exact only for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class, whose simultaneous parallel-trends clause is stronger than the source's per-dose wording. The inference theorem additionally fixes a known finite rectangle union, \(\beta\), a uniform positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation, and uses a conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed-measure control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation without density smoothness, strict feasibility, or optimizer uniqueness. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). A matching lower bound as \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\) remains open; shrinking-hole asymptotics require a new varying-support class.
body.honest_scope: The negative conclusion is exact for the published class at the regular witness: its legal affine recession ray generates all of \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The finite set \(\Theta(P)\) is instead the sharp causal set for a strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class with a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), and a simultaneous common-event diagonal clause. Marginal quasi-stayers are unnecessary for that sensitivity characterization. No global equality or inclusion with the source class is claimed, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 concerns unweighted \(\delta_1\); and the common-zero-baseline scalar bounds in arXiv:2405.04465v4 are prior art. The source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged. Uniform outer inference is confined to the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, density-bounded-below, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. No lower-bound optimality result is claimed; support-topology asymptotics, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length are also outside scope.
